newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Prices up, anticipates fresh demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Prices up, anticipates fresh demand.

text.p: Anticipations that fresh purchase could emerge in the high sulphur fuel oil market in the near term provided strong support for prices on Monday, traders said.
A bid for the 180-cst grade went up to $102.50 per tonne from an earlier $102.00 while an offer was heard at $104.50.
Some traders speculated that a local trader, who bought one cargo last week at $102.00 per tonne, would bid up prices to coincide with the arrival of a large cargo from the Gulf.
"People are guessing and hoping but no one is sure whether the local trader will continue to bid up," said another trader. The 380-cst grade was offered at $95.00, traders said.
Last Friday, the 180-cst grade was offered at $102.50 per tonne for late May delivery. It was traded at $102.00 per tonne for May 26-30 delivery on Thursday.
In the swaps market, June was at $101.50/$102.50 against Friday's $102.00/$103.00 and July was at $100.25/$101.50 against $100.50/$101.50.

Amid fewer Middle East cargoes coming to Asia as the summer season nears, two cargoes were traded last week with the second cargo sold $2 per tonne higher than the first one, reflecting a a firm market undertone, traders said.

They said higher summer demand for air-conditioning in the Middle East and maintenance turnarounds in South Korea in May and June are expected to tighten supplies in the second half of May. They said this would give prices a further boosts.
"The fundamentals are giving a hand to those who want to bid up the market," said one trader.
The market is also watching tender results of the Korean Electric Power Company (KEPCO) to buy two cargoes of 70,000-tonne, 540-centistoke fuel oil for July delivery, traders said.
The tender for 0.3-percent fuel oil will close on May 16 and is valid for three days.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
